top.title: Kyle Whittingham Makes Bold Statement Following Michigan’s Stunning Victory
top.description: Kyle Whittingham celebrated his 67th birthday Saturday with a victory he won’t soon forget. Michigan’s embattled head coach watched his Wolverines stun previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA 18-16 in triple overtime, securing bowl eligibility and delivering one of the biggest upsets of the college football season. But when Whittingham stepped in front of reporters following the game, he wasn’t interested in making the moment about himself. Instead, he immediately turned his attention to Michigan’s seniors, who had just played their final game at The Big House. Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham reacts to a play against UCLA during the first half at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. Despite Michigan’s struggles, Whittingham made it clear that his appreciation for the team hasn’t wavered. “I’m so proud of those guys, love this football team, a bunch of great guys, great guys to coach, to be around, and it was, like I said, a big point of emphasis. And to see that happen was so gratifying to see that.” Michigan entered Saturday’s matchup needing one more victory to become bowl eligible, a difficult assignment against an undefeated UCLA squad. It was a fitting conclusion to Senior Day, particularly considering the number of close games Michigan had failed to finish earlier in the year. top.title: CBA breezes into the Class AA state semifinals after routing Valley Central
top.description: CBA senior JT Vogel, left, and sophomore Jacob Turner celebrate after Vogel blocked a punt and Turner returned it for a touchdown during the Class AA state quarterfinals against Valley Central on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in Colonie, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) COLONIE - One carry, one touchdown. A second carry, another touchdown. A third carry, a third touchdown. Then, the offense for the Christian Brothers Academy football team actually slowed down during its fourth possession Saturday, as the Brothers required three plays to reach the end zone that time. The state's No. 3-ranked Class AA squad displayed its overall prowess once again, this time blasting Section 9 champion Valley Central 69-6 in state quarterfinal play at Colonie High School. CBA (12-0) ran the ball four times during the opening quarter and scored touchdowns on each attempt. In all, the Brothers amassed 263 yards of offense over six plays in the first quarter, which ended with the Brothers ahead 28-0. "It felt good to play like that," said CBA junior two-way standout Jack Hulett, who was named his team's Offensive Player of the Game. "Coach (Bobby) Burns and the rest of the staff got us prepared pretty well for what we needed to do. We came out and played hard." The Brothers produced a resounding 61-14 triumph over Saratoga Springs in the Section 2 Class AA Super Bowl to secure a fifth sectional title since 2021. There was absolutely zero letdown Saturday, as CBA senior running back Tommy Toher opened the scoring festivities by dashing 80 yards for a touchdown on the first play from scrimmage. That score started a streak of three consecutive plays from scrimmage that saw the CBA offense score a touchdown. "Monday, we flipped the script from Saratoga to this game," Hulett said. "This is a highly motivated group. They are locked in," Burns said. "They want to get back to the (JMA Wireless Dome in Syracuse) for the state final and want to get it done. That is the motivation." Hulett, a junior who stars at receiver and safety, proceeded to help make it 21-0 as he generated touchdown runs covering 79 and 60 yards, respectively. Toher's second touch of the game resulted in a 4-yard touchdown run with 1:33 left in the first quarter. The Brothers added four more touchdowns in the second quarter to lead 55-0 at intermission. "When we execute, we have special players that can do special things," Burns said. "All the work we have put in is paying off. We are now looking to next week and trying to get better in order to reach the Dome," Hulett said. The CBA starters had the second half off. The Brothers' reserves moved the ball efficiently over the final 24 minutes, featuring some strong runs by Brady Munsinger and Tyrone Barrow. Jacob Turner, a sophomore who scooped up a blocked punt and scored a touchdown in the second quarter, returned a kickoff 88 yards for a touchdown in the fourth quarter. top.title: Blackhawks Captain Connor Bedard Will Undergo Right Shoulder Surgery
top.description: The Chicago Blackhawks should be riding high after earning their first road win of the 2026-27 regular season against the Calgary Flames on Saturday night. But it’s hard to celebrate too much when the star player and team captain is now facing another extended absence. After Saturday’s win, general manager Kyle Davidson told the media that Connor Bedard has decided to undergo surgery to repair his right shoulder. Bedard, the Blackhawks team doctors, and outside experts have recently been weighing the pros and cons of rehab vs. surgery for his latest injury . We now know his choice. Breaking: Connor Bedard is getting shoulder surgery, Kyle Davidson says. — Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) November 22, 2026 Bedard suffered the injury in Tuesday’s 6-3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs , while battling with Leafs center Nick Paul at the faceoff circle. Last December, Bedard injured his right shoulder in similar circumstances, getting tangled up with then-St. Louis Blues captain Brayden Schenn while trying to win a faceoff. Bedard chose rehab over surgery last winter and returned to the Blackhawks roughly four weeks later, missing 12 games. But after suffering the same injury again, his second serious right shoulder injury in 11 months, the risk of re-injury or doing further damage without surgery appeared to be too much. The 21-year-old will undergo surgery this week, marking his second shoulder procedure in under five months. Bedard had left shoulder surgery on July 8 stemming from a freak accident during offseason training in Vancouver. He returned to the Blackhawks on Oct. 13 after missing the first six games of the 2026-27 season. Davidson told the traveling media that Bedard’s upcoming right shoulder surgery will likely be the same procedure he had on his left shoulder in July. Dr. Peter Millett, the surgeon who repaired Bedard’s left shoulder this past summer, will also repair his right shoulder. Bedard’s return timeline won’t be determined until after surgery, per Davidson, but it will likely be between 3-4 months. For his left shoulder, Bedard was initially given a four-month recovery timeline, but he returned in just over three months. That puts Bedard on track to potentially return in mid-to-late February, at the earliest. However, considering this will be his second serious procedure in such a short stretch, the Blackhawks will presumably be extra cautious with the face of the franchise. While it’s another devastating development for the Blackhawks early this season, and as difficult as the decision must have been for Bedard, he made the correct one. Electing to do rehab again and returning with a banged-up shoulder is a risk neither he nor the Blackhawks could afford. A third injury could have led to dire consequences and created serious long-term issues. As the prized jewel of the rebuild, Bedard had to nip this in the bud, right here, right now. top.description: STATE COLLEGE, Pa. — Rutgers fulfilled Greg Schiano’s promise that it would win a game that no one expected after all. Behind a starting quarterback playing with three broken ribs and a defense that ranked among the worst in the country, the Scarlet Knights stunned Penn State in a 25-24 victory that snapped a decades-long losing streak and rewarded the school’s decision to maintain its maligned head coach for the eighth season of his second stint. top.title: Cowboys' CeeDee Lamb punished by the NFL before Titans game
top.description: Cowboys' CeeDee Lamb punished by the NFL before Titans game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NFL season is already reaching its later stages, and it's crunch time for the Dallas Cowboys . If this team wants to make the playoffs, it's going to have to start winning and keep it up for the rest of the season. That starts Sunday when the Cowboys take on the Titans at home. Now, one of the team's biggest offensive stars, CeeDee Lamb, is getting punished by the NFL ahead of the matchup. CeeDee Lamb receives the biggest fine of the week after helmet-related penalty against the 49ers Every week during the season, the NFL announces fines on Saturday for games played the week before. So, the league's Week 10 punishments are out. "The rules are intended to protect the players from unnecessary risk, promote player safety and emphasize sportsmanship and respect of teammates, opponents, coaches, officials and fans," the NFL notes on its official website . As you can probably guess, Lamb was slapped with a fine this week for actions during the team's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers . The NFL is fining Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb $23,882 for unnecessary roughness after he was flagged for using his helmet. The fine stems from a block on 49ers cornerback Deommodore Lenoir during George Pickens' 39-yard touchdown reception. Although officials initially flagged the play before picking up the penalty, the NFL reviewed the footage and determined that Lamb violated its helmet-use rules. That $23,882 figure is actually the biggest fine of the week, so it may be enough to convince Lamb to think twice before making that kind of play again. top.title: Trinity Rodman appears to injure shoulder, stays in NWSL Championship
top.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. — Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman went down clutching her left shoulder early in the 2026 NWSL Championship after a hard foul committed by the Kansas City Current on Saturday, Nov. 21. Current defender Laney Rouse collied with Rodman in the air at the five-minute mark of the championship game. Rodman remained down on the pitch in visible pain as a cascade of boos rained down from the home crowd at Audi Field. After a momentary delay, play continued as Rodman was tended to on the sidelines. After stretching her left arm and doing several arm circles, Rodman checked back into the game in the sixth minute to a loud applause, although she still appeared to be in some discomfort. The contact didn’t result in a card for Rouse, but the first yellow card of the game was handed out several minutes later when the Current’s Michelle Cooper was shown one for a hard foul on the Spirit’s Leicy Santos in the ninth minute. NWSL Championship live: Washington Spirit vs. Kansas City Current score, highlights Rodman has dealt with numerous injuries throughout her star-studded career, particularly in the Spirit's past two championship game appearances, which resulted in losses for Washington in 2024 and 2025. Rodman played through a sprained MCL in her right knee in the Spirit's 1-0 loss to Gotham FC in 2025, while a lingering back issue impacted her performance in the Spirit's 1-0 loss to the Orlando Pride in 2024. After being limited to a career-low 17 matches last season due to back and knee injuries, she bounced back with a career year this season that included personal highs in both goals (14), assists (10) and games played (33). "It makes me want to cry," Rodman said. "Just being able to be available, I don't think people realize how much of a blessing it is to be healthy enough to play. And I don't think you realize that until you go through something where it keeps you from doing something you love to do." top.title: Messi, Miami stunned by Columbus in MLS playoff opener
top.description: Columbus Crew's Gonzalo Tapia celebrates after scoring his second goal in a 3-0 win over Lionel Messi's Inter Miami (JC Ruiz) Lionel Messi's bid to win back-to-back MLS Cup titles suffered a blow on Saturday as 10-man Inter Miami were thumped 3-0 at home by Columbus Crew in their first-round playoff series opener. Two goals from Chile international Gonzalo Tapia either side of a Taha Habroune second-half strike secured a deserved victory for Crew in front of a shellshocked crowd at Miami's Nu Stadium. The result means seventh seeds Columbus, the 2023 champions, can eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in game two of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday. On Saturday's evidence, Columbus will head into game two confident of finishing the job after tearing Miami to shreds. The 24-year-old Tapia was a menace throughout, winning an early penalty after being brought down by Miami goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair before stepping up to convert the spot-kick. Miami's task got harder in the 36th minute when Gonzalo Lujan was sent off after receiving a second yellow card for a reckless late challenge on the Crew's Stephen Moreira. Columbus's US international goalkeeper Patrick Schulte, meanwhile, thwarted Miami's attempts to get back in the game, including one diving save to deny Messi a trademark free-kick. Messi was fortunate to escape dismissal on half-time, when he appeared to direct a throw-in into Tapia's face at point-blank range as frustrations boiled over. Columbus made the game safe early in the second half with two goals in six minutes. A fine flowing counter-attack ended with Harbroune coolly slotting past St.Clair in the 52nd minute before Tapia made it 3-0 in the 58th minute, punishing slack marking by Miami's Yannick Bright to go clean through on goal. "It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them," Miami coach Kily Gonzalez said afterwards. "We didn't produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don't win, we're out," he added. "There's no better challenge for us as a team than this. It's a test of character, and I know my team has that character." In other MLS playoff action on Saturday, Joaquin Valiente scored two goals as host Dallas beat Portland 3-0 in their Western Conference series opener. The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder scored in the 53rd and 55th minutes and Samuel Sarver added an insurance goal in the fourth minute of stoppage time for Dallas, who can advance by winning at Portland next Saturday. US teen Peyton Miller scored one goal and set up another in New England's 2-0 victory over visiting Philadelphia. top.description: Carlie Cisneros (12) — TUCSON, ARIZ. -- Volleyball vs. Grand Canyon University at McKale Center at ALKEME Arena. Aug. 19, 2026. | Photo by Marison Bilagody / Arizona Athletics The Arizona Wildcats have taken sets off or played very competitive three-setters against teams ranked 10th, 11th, 14th, and 32nd in the RPI during Big 12 play. On Saturday, No. 40 Utah was on the schedule. Once again, it was a competitive match that ended in a 3-1 (25-18, 22-25, 25-21, 26-24) loss. “Other than how we started off the set, the first set—I wasn’t too happy with that—I thought we did a good job of staying competitive on the floor,” Arizona head coach Rita Stubbs said. “Unfortunately, our skills broke down in certain situations, and coachability wasn’t necessarily the best, and they took advantage of it at the right time, but the wrong time for us.” Arizona was especially done in by Utah runs later in sets. That was even the case in the second set, which the Wildcats won. UA went up 19-12 in the second only to have the Utes go on a five-point run to close the lead to two. The big cushion was the saving grace for the Wildcats. They were able to trade points and mini-runs with Utah down the stretch to win by three points. Those mid- and late-set runs were their downfall in the third and fourth sets. It didn’t take a lot in sets that were so closely contested. The difference in the third came with the teams tied at 12. Utah went on a three-point run to reach the technical timeout leading 15-12. It never trailed again. Another three-point run later in the set gave the Utes set point at 24-19. Arizona saved two set points, but it was just one of five occasions when it scored more than one point in a row. Four of those five “runs” were of just two points and the other was three. The fourth was a back-and-forth affair throughout as Arizona fought to stay in the match. The Wildcats took their first lead at 7-6 and had a four-point lead at the technical timeout. Stubbs called time and Arizona responded with a 4-0 run to go up 21-17. The Wildcats were so close to evening the match. Once again, the timeout changed the teams’ fortunes. top.title: 'Baltimore isn't a talking point to me': Carmelo Anthony calls out Marlon Humphrey
top.description: Credit: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images, Brad Penner-Imagn Images Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey made the wrong kind of headlines this past week after making a joke on his podcast at the expense of the city he represents on the field. During an episode of his podcast, The Marlon Humphrey Show , Humphrey was asked what Baltimore was best at making, and responded, “criminals,” with a laugh. Given that Humphrey has played for the Ravens for a decade, the remark quickly made the rounds as fans and media alike expressed their disappointment. Humphrey has since apologized, but was sent home for the week by the team and will be inactive for Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers as a punishment for the comments. He has also been on the receiving end of critiques from the likes of Shannon Sharpe and Kevin Wildes , who suggested maybe it was time for him to stop podcasting. On Friday, former NBA star and current analyst Carmelo Anthony joined the voices of those calling out Humphrey. Anthony, who played his high school basketball in the Baltimore area, sent a clear message to Humphrey via a series of posts to his Instagram account. “Listen. I’ve been sitting with this one for a couple of days, because Baltimore isn’t a talking point to me. It’s my blood,” Anthony wrote. “I came up on Myrtle Avenue in West Baltimore. I saw what this city can take from you. I lost friends to the streets, and I watched people I loved get swallowed by a system that was built to swallow them. I know the reputation. I’ve heard every joke and every headline my whole life. “So when one of our own stands on our name and says the best thing Baltimore makes is criminals, and then laughs that it’ll get cut out, that doesn’t get cut out for me. It doesn’t get cut out for the kid in Baltimore who heard it. It doesn’t get cut out for the mother working two jobs to keep her son off the corner. And it doesn’t get cut out for the man who did his time, came home, and is fighting every day to be seen as more than his worst moment.” Anthony acknowledged Humphrey’s apology, but challenged him to get more involved in the local community and engage with the city and its people. “You don’t get to rep Baltimore on Sunday and talk about it like an outsider on Wednesday,” he wrote. Anthony closed out his message by asking that Humphrey make good on an invitation that Baltimore mayor Brandon Scott made to him to meet with residents who are working to make the city a better place and keep others from making the mistakes of their past. top.description: Michigan tight end Jalen Hoffman (42) makes a catch for the game-winning 2-point conversion against UCLA during the third overtime at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. ANN ARBOR, Mich. — UCLA traveled to Ann Arbor searching for a historic win. A victory would secure the program's first 11-win season, tie the school mark for single-season conference victories and clinch a berth in the Big Ten championship game. All UCLA had to do was defeat Michigan in The Big House. Instead, the fourth-ranked Bruins walked off the turf in defeat for the first time this season, falling to the Wolverines 18-16 in triple overtime on Saturday at Michigan Stadium. “This was a battle, and obviously we came up a little bit short," head coach Bob Chesney said postgame. "We have to find a way to get better, period." Not only did UCLA watch a chance at an undefeated season and a potential trip to Indianapolis slip away in heartbreaking fashion, it also lost its starting quarterback. After marching down the field on a 15-play, 77-yard drive to tie the game with 10 seconds remaining on a jump-pass touchdown from Anthony Woods to Brayden Loftin, UCLA headed to overtime deadlocked at 10, looking to add another chapter to a remarkable campaign. On the first snap of overtime, senior quarterback Ty Dieffenbach scrambled to his right and was brought down by Michigan defender Troy Bowles for a 6-yard gain. Dieffenbach remained down on the play, appearing in serious pain before being carted off the field. nigeria.title: Why construction could become Africa’s key technology, investment opportunity
nigeria.description: By Jimoh Razaq For years, Africa’s technology ecosystem has concentrated much of its entrepreneurial energy, investment capital and innovation around fintech, e-commerce, mobility, telecommunications and entertainment. These sectors have produced remarkable companies, attracted international investment and demonstrated that African businesses can build technology products capable of scaling across borders. But there is another industry with enormous economic significance, deeply entrenched inefficiencies and a largely untapped opportunity for technological transformation: construction. It is an industry that builds our homes, roads, hospitals, schools, factories, power infrastructure and cities. It employs millions of people, supports extensive manufacturing and distribution networks, moves significant volumes of capital and sits at the centre of economic development. Yet much of its operational infrastructure remains fragmented, manual and inefficient. While technology has transformed how people transfer money, order food, book transportation and access entertainment, the processes through which buildings and infrastructure are planned, financed, procured and delivered remain remarkably difficult to coordinate. This is not simply an operational inconvenience. It is a massive economic opportunity. The next generation of transformative African technology companies may emerge from solving the problems of the industries that physically build Africa. McKinsey’s 2024 research found that global construction productivity grew by approximately 0.4 per cent annually between 2000 and 2022, compared with around 2 per cent for the broader economy. nigeria.title: PSHAN, WHO urge increased private investment to rescue Nigeria’s healthcare system
nigeria.description: By Matthew Johnson The Private Sector Health Alliance of Nigeria (PSHAN) and the World Health Organisation (WHO) have called for increased private sector investment and stronger public-private partnerships to address persistent challenges confronting Nigeria’s healthcare system. The organisations said government alone could not shoulder the responsibility of transforming the health sector, stressing that sustained private sector investment was critical to improving healthcare delivery, strengthening infrastructure and achieving universal health coverage. The call was made at the 2026 PSHAN Annual Gala and Awards Night held in Lagos on November 20, with the theme, “Legacy Builders: Honouring the Visionaries of the Nigerian Healthcare System.” Speaking at the event, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of PSHAN, Dr. Tinuola Akinbolagbe, said the alliance was working to position the private sector at the centre of Nigeria’s health development through strategic partnerships, investment, innovation and institutional strengthening. She said PSHAN was seeking to move beyond fragmented private sector interventions towards coordinated investments capable of strengthening health systems and delivering measurable and sustainable outcomes. According to her, meaningful progress in healthcare requires shared responsibility and collaboration across different sectors. “As we look towards 2027 and beyond, our ambition is to move from fragmented contributions by the private sector to coordinated investment, from isolated interventions to stronger health systems, and from good intentions to measurable, sustainable outcomes,” she said. Akinbolagbe explained that the theme of the event was designed to celebrate individuals, institutions and organisations whose courage, leadership, innovation and commitment had contributed to shaping the future of healthcare in Nigeria. In his keynote address, former President of the African Development Bank Group and Executive Chairman of the Global Africa Investment Summit, Dr. Akinwumi Adesina, described healthcare as an investment in human capital and essential economic infrastructure rather than merely social sector expenditure. Speaking on the theme, “Health as Wealth: Mobilising African Leadership and Capital to Build Sustainable Health Systems,” Adesina said a healthy population was fundamental to productivity, innovation, economic competitiveness and national prosperity. He maintained that no country could achieve sustainable wealth without a healthy population, insisting that investment in healthcare was essential to building a productive workforce and inclusive economy. Adesina called for stronger partnerships between government and the private sector, noting that government alone could not finance and deliver the transformation required in the country’s healthcare system. He urged businesses to move beyond philanthropy and corporate social responsibility initiatives to embrace healthcare as a strategic investment

nigeria.title: Anambra’s Ekwulobia flyover to be commissioned November 27
nigeria.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Anambra State Executive Council has fixed November 27, 2026, for the formal commissioning and opening of the Ekwulobia flyover constructed by the administration of Governor Chukwuma Soludo. The flyover is strategically located at a junction that previously experienced serious traffic challenges, particularly during festive periods when vehicular movement increases significantly. Rising from its meeting in Awka, the State Executive Council directed that all necessary arrangements be made to ensure a successful and hitch-free commissioning. However, it did not disclose who would perform the ceremony. The state Commissioner for Information and Value Reorientation, Dr Law Mefor, described the flyover as one of the flagship urban regeneration projects of the Soludo administration. He said the project stood alongside the transformation of Okpoko, formerly regarded as the biggest urban slum in the South-East, into an area characterised by improved infrastructure, order and human dignity. “These projects underscore Governor Soludo’s irreversible commitment to building a liveable, prosperous and smart mega-city in Anambra State,” Mefor said. Meanwhile, the Council resolved to move the state’s Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) drive from moral suasion to full enforcement, including the prosecution of tax evaders, to maximise the state’s revenue potential. It consequently urged residents, business owners and other taxpayers to pay their taxes and levies promptly to avoid the consequences of enforcement, particularly prosecution. According to the Council, no modern state can be built on voluntary compliance alone, stressing that payment of taxes is a civic responsibility. “Anambra will enforce it fairly and firmly,” the Council said. The Council also disclosed that it had concluded work on the state’s 2027 budget, which Governor Soludo is expected to present to the Anambra State House of Assembly on Tuesday. Mefor described the proposed budget as a consolidation budget designed to deepen the gains of Solution 2.0 in infrastructure, security, education, healthcare, youth empowerment and economic transformation. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. Read the full recipe for Rice and Peas with Oxtail . Rice and peas with oxtail, from Episode 1 Soliat Bada and Michael Famoroti in Episode 1 Episode 2 moves to the Gulf for lamb kabsa, Saudi Arabia’s national dish, fragrant with dried lime and seven spice. Soliat is joined by Bella Adeleke , CEO of Asali Africa and founder of the fashion label Garbe, for a conversation about redefining success. Read the full recipe for Lamb Kabsa . Lamb kabsa, from Episode 2 Still to come are Nigerian fried rice with fried turkey and dodo, cooked with Toyin Jolapamo and Nneoma Mere; jambalaya with Goldie Iyamu and Vanessa Iloenyosi ; and a season finale with Edwin Okolo and Temi Omolehinwa. For more on Asali Africa and the products and ideas it develops, visit asali.africa . Episodes 1 and 2 are out now on YouTube. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. Market scale does not, on its own, define technology leadership. What it does provide is evidence that a manufacturer has become an important participant in how the category develops. For a company operating at that scale, leadership increasingly includes helping make the technology easier to understand and giving consumers clearer ways to evaluate what they are buying. entertainment.title: A Safari, a Beach & Easy Entry? 5 African Spots for Your Christmas Holiday
entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. Rwanda Not everyone wants their year-end holiday to feel like a non-stop sprint, and Rwanda is built for travellers who prefer scenery, clean air, and an unhurried pace. Days in Kigali easily revolve around specialty coffee shops, contemporary art at Inema Arts Center, and a sobering, essential visit to the Kigali Genocide Memorial before you head out into the countryside. From the capital, you can track chimpanzees and walk above the trees in Nyungwe Forest, go on wildlife drives in Akagera National Park, or spend quiet afternoons along the shores of Lake Kivu. With 30-day visa-free entry for Nigerian passport holders, getting there is straightforward from start to finish. Mauritius Sometimes a proper Christmas break calls for leaving mainland schedules behind altogether for turquoise lagoons, catamaran cruises, and mountain trails. In Mauritius, you can base yourself around Grand Baie in the north for boat trips to Île aux Cerfs and lively beachside dinners, or head south-west toward Le Morne Brabant for coastal hikes and water sports. Between beach days, the bustling Central Market in Port Louis, the lush trails of Black River Gorges National Park, and Casela Nature Parks keep a week-long itinerary full without ever feeling hectic. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. entertainment.title: How La Roche-Posay Brought Skin Science to Over 500 Guests in Its First Living Lab Experience
entertainment.description: La Roche-Posay concluded its first Living Lab experience in Nigeria, welcoming Nigerian stakeholders to its opening party and three-day programme, held from 4 to 6 November 2026 at Oasis by The Five Palm, Victoria Island, Lagos. Inspired by the original Living Lab concept in Paris, the experience brought the science, research and expertise behind skincare closer to Nigerian consumers and healthcare professionals. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Each space introduced visitors to specific skin concerns and the science behind the brand’s product formulations. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. At the Anthelios corner, visitors used a UV camera to see the effects of ultraviolet exposure and better understand the importance of sun protection. The Effaclar and Mela B3 spaces explored concerns including blemishes and hyperpigmentation, while the Cicaplast and Lipikar corners introduced visitors to approaches to caring for sensitive, damaged and dry skin. Beyond the Innovation Corners, visitors explored the Blue House, which presented La Roche-Posay’s history and commitment to dermatological innovation, and the Scars of Life Cinema. The cinema screened a 25-minute film exploring the physical and psychological realities of living with scars and scarring, including their impact on self-image and everyday life. The film also highlighted how Lipikar supports the care of skin affected by scarring, bringing attention to the importance of addressing both the visible and less visible experiences associated with skin conditions. The programme also created opportunities for visitors to engage with skincare experts and dermatologists through one-on-one consultations, ask questions about their individual skin concerns and receive guidance on building appropriate skincare routines. entertainment.description: One of the best aspects of art is its ability to imitate current events or imagine possibilities. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. At its core, art exists to entertain, inform and critique society. Through films, music and visual expressions, we are continually reminded of our shared humanity—our joys, flaws and contradictions. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Nonetheless, some films have attempted to explore what it means to be a man in today’s world. They invite audiences to contemplate important questions such as: What is the role of men in society? What defines a man? How does a man’s behaviour influence those around him? What expectations does society place on men? What responsibilities do men have within society? Through his struggles with homelessness, rejection, and exhaustion, the film redefines masculinity, depicting it as the courage to remain tender even when life tests your strength in every way. entertainment.title: Ibukun Awosika, Juliet Ibrahim, Bola Adesola & More: Leading Women Take Centre Stage at The Executive Woman Summit 2.0
entertainment.description: What does it really mean to play to win in business and leadership? Beyond earning a seat at the table, it requires more than competence or professional accomplishments. It requires the confidence to own one’s value, the clarity to communicate one’s contributions and the intentionality to build visibility that translates into meaningful influence. These conversations defined The Executive Woman Summit (TEWS) 2.0 , which brought together hundreds of executive women, corporate professionals, entrepreneurs and emerging leaders at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. Convened by Bola Matel-Okoh , a dual-qualified attorney (called to both the New York and Nigerian Bars), Executive Coach, Non-Executive Director at Wema Bank, and CEO of BMO Advisory Services , the second edition of the summit was themed Playing to Win: Elevate Your Vision, Value and Visibility. It provided an intentional platform for candid conversations, practical insights and strategic alliances on what it takes for women to advance, lead and thrive in today’s evolving corporate landscape. In her opening address, Matel-Okoh challenged women to rethink how they approach professional visibility, authority and advancement. According to her, competence is merely the baseline; it is not enough if you are unwilling to communicate your value, own your voice and position yourself for higher-stakes opportunities. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. sports.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. — Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman went down clutching her left shoulder early in the 2026 NWSL Championship after a hard foul committed by the Kansas City Current on Saturday, Nov. 21. The 24-year-old Tapia was a menace throughout, winning an early penalty after being brought down by Miami goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair before stepping up to convert the spot-kick. Messi was fortunate to escape dismissal on half-time, when he appeared to direct a throw-in into Tapia's face at point-blank range as frustrations boiled over. Columbus made the game safe early in the second half with two goals in six minutes. "It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them," Miami coach Kily Gonzalez said afterwards. sports.title: 'Baltimore isn't a talking point to me': Carmelo Anthony calls out Marlon Humphrey
sports.description: Credit: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images, Brad Penner-Imagn Images Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey made the wrong kind of headlines this past week after making a joke on his podcast at the expense of the city he represents on the field. During an episode of his podcast, The Marlon Humphrey Show , Humphrey was asked what Baltimore was best at making, and responded, “criminals,” with a laugh. Given that Humphrey has played for the Ravens for a decade, the remark quickly made the rounds as fans and media alike expressed their disappointment. Humphrey has since apologized, but was sent home for the week by the team and will be inactive for Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers as a punishment for the comments. He has also been on the receiving end of critiques from the likes of Shannon Sharpe and Kevin Wildes , who suggested maybe it was time for him to stop podcasting. On Friday, former NBA star and current analyst Carmelo Anthony joined the voices of those calling out Humphrey. Anthony, who played his high school basketball in the Baltimore area, sent a clear message to Humphrey via a series of posts to his Instagram account. “Listen. I’ve been sitting with this one for a couple of days, because Baltimore isn’t a talking point to me. It’s my blood,” Anthony wrote. “I came up on Myrtle Avenue in West Baltimore. I saw what this city can take from you. I lost friends to the streets, and I watched people I loved get swallowed by a system that was built to swallow them. I know the reputation. I’ve heard every joke and every headline my whole life. “So when one of our own stands on our name and says the best thing Baltimore makes is criminals, and then laughs that it’ll get cut out, that doesn’t get cut out for me. It doesn’t get cut out for the kid in Baltimore who heard it. It doesn’t get cut out for the mother working two jobs to keep her son off the corner. And it doesn’t get cut out for the man who did his time, came home, and is fighting every day to be seen as more than his worst moment.” Anthony acknowledged Humphrey’s apology, but challenged him to get more involved in the local community and engage with the city and its people. “You don’t get to rep Baltimore on Sunday and talk about it like an outsider on Wednesday,” he wrote. Anthony closed out his message by asking that Humphrey make good on an invitation that Baltimore mayor Brandon Scott made to him to meet with residents who are working to make the city a better place and keep others from making the mistakes of their past. sports.title: Michigan upsets No. 4 UCLA 18-16 in triple overtime, ending Bruins' unbeaten season
sports.description: Michigan tight end Jalen Hoffman (42) makes a catch for the game-winning 2-point conversion against UCLA during the third overtime at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. ANN ARBOR, Mich. — UCLA traveled to Ann Arbor searching for a historic win. A victory would secure the program's first 11-win season, tie the school mark for single-season conference victories and clinch a berth in the Big Ten championship game. All UCLA had to do was defeat Michigan in The Big House. Instead, the fourth-ranked Bruins walked off the turf in defeat for the first time this season, falling to the Wolverines 18-16 in triple overtime on Saturday at Michigan Stadium. “This was a battle, and obviously we came up a little bit short," head coach Bob Chesney said postgame. "We have to find a way to get better, period." Not only did UCLA watch a chance at an undefeated season and a potential trip to Indianapolis slip away in heartbreaking fashion, it also lost its starting quarterback. After marching down the field on a 15-play, 77-yard drive to tie the game with 10 seconds remaining on a jump-pass touchdown from Anthony Woods to Brayden Loftin, UCLA headed to overtime deadlocked at 10, looking to add another chapter to a remarkable campaign. On the first snap of overtime, senior quarterback Ty Dieffenbach scrambled to his right and was brought down by Michigan defender Troy Bowles for a 6-yard gain. Dieffenbach remained down on the play, appearing in serious pain before being carted off the field. Nov 21, 2026; Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA; UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach (14) reacts after an injury in overtime at Michigan Stadium. Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Nov 21, 2026; Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA; UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach (14) reacts after an injury in overtime at Michigan Stadium. Backup Madden Iamaleava took over under center and struggled to move the ball against a standout Michigan defense, failing to complete a pass while hesitating on multiple scrambles in crucial moments. The most glaring miscue came on third-and-6 from the Michigan 21-yard line, when Iamaleava stepped up in the pocket with a wide-open lane to move the chains. The sophomore failed to capitalize on the defensive breakdown and was tripped up short of the first-down marker. Both teams traded field goals in the first two overtimes, setting up a sudden-death battle of two-point conversion plays tied at 16. The Bruins came up empty on their two-point attempt, with Iamaleava unable to get a pass away after spinning to his left. One play later, Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood delivered the decisive blow, rolling to his right and finding Jalen Hoffman in the end zone for the game-winner, handing UCLA its first defeat and sending Michigan fans storming onto the field in celebration. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). It's a masterclass showcasing the ever-brilliant Stewart's impressive range, as the out-of-control captain's rarely seen temper reaches fever pitch, before normal service is resumed. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. And just as the franchise's zenith, "The Wrath of Khan", is built around Kirk and Khan's decades-old feud, "First Contact" is precision engineered to get the most out of Jean-Luc. This was the right "Star Trek" at the right time, a film that put "TNG"'s greatest villains on a collision course with the origins of Starfleet. science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
science.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. "The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind , to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description . "The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.

The Falcon 9 has been putting up incredible numbers lately — it flew a whopping 165 times in 2025 , for example — but the workhorse rocket is on its way out . science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. science.description: null On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station. Today, the I nternational Space Station is about the size of a football field and typically hosts up to seven crewmembers. But back in 1998, it was a pretty tight squeeze. It is a marvel of space engineering, but every engineering marvel begins the same: with the first piece. And that is what the Zarya module is: The foundation of the International Space Station. Zarya, also known as the Functional Cargo Block (or Russian acronym FGB), is the core module of the space station around which every other module was attached. It weighed 42,600 pounds at launch and is just aver 41 feet long and 13.5 feet wide. Inside, it boasts a total habitable volume of 1,650 cubic feet. science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

Awards to small businesses around the country are addressing some of NASA’s most crucial technology needs for exploration of the Moon and Mars while fueling the U.S. space economy. NASA’s Small Business Innovation Research/Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) program recently selected 302 innovative projects, for a total investment of up to $171 million in seed funding. Selected projects include next-generation battery solutions, robotic systems with sensing capabilities for the extreme lunar environment, and tools to prepare for construction of critical infrastructure, such as lunar landing pads. Working with the program, a company’s path toward commercialization or infusion into NASA missions occurs in phases. The latest awards involved two of these phases. The new Phase I contracts will receive up to $225,000 each to establish the merit and feasibility of their proposed innovation. A portion of the projects selected are STTR awards, provided to small businesses partnered with research institutions. The Phase II awards, with 98 contracts valued at up to $1.3 million each, will continue work begun in Phase I projects selected in 2025, targeting demonstration and delivery of the innovative technologies. science.title: GTA hasn't gone to space (yet), but these sci-fi games can offer you a life of crime among the stars
science.description: GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time . Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans? To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space. The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons. The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games. With new hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars. Roleplaying a space outlaw (Image credit: Bethesda Softworks) Massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics. Starfield even has a "new game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it. (Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining. Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky .
